summary: At Jesus’ presentation in the temple, aged Simeon takes Him in his arms and praises God for His salvation; the prophetess Anna speaks of Him to all awaiting redemption.
key_insight: Simeon is the first in Luke to say two things aloud about Jesus: that He is salvation for the Gentiles as well as for Israel, and that He will be “a sign which will be spoken against.” Joy and sorrow are announced together, over a baby about six weeks old.
story: When the days of Mary’s purification under the law of Moses were completed, Joseph and Mary brought Jesus to Jerusalem to present Him to the Lord. The law said, “Every male who opens the womb shall be called holy to the LORD.” They also offered the sacrifice the law allowed, “A pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons.”

In Jerusalem lived a man named Simeon, just and devout, “waiting for the Consolation of Israel,” and the Holy Spirit was upon him. The Spirit had shown him that he would not die before he had seen the Lord’s Christ. Led by the Spirit, he came into the temple just as Jesus’ parents brought Him in.

Simeon took the Child in his arms and blessed God: “Lord, now You are letting Your servant depart in peace, according to Your word; for my eyes have seen Your salvation which You have prepared before the face of all peoples, a light to bring revelation to the Gentiles, and the glory of Your people Israel.”

Joseph and Mary marveled at what was said about Him. Simeon blessed them and said to Mary, “Behold, this Child is destined for the fall and rising of many in Israel, and for a sign which will be spoken against (yes, a sword will pierce through your own soul also), that the thoughts of many hearts may be revealed.”

There was also a prophetess, Anna, the daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Asher. She had lived with her husband seven years after her marriage and had been a widow ever since, and now she was of a great age. She never left the temple but served God with fastings and prayers night and day. Coming up at that very moment, she gave thanks to the Lord and spoke of Him to all who looked for redemption in Jerusalem.

scene.label: Purification and presentation
scene.text: After a son’s birth, a mother waited forty days before she could enter the sanctuary, and then brought an offering (Leviticus 12:2–6). Every firstborn son belonged to the Lord and was redeemed for five shekels (Exodus 13:2; Numbers 18:15–16). Luke brings the two together in one visit.

scene.label: The offering of the poor
scene.text: The law asked for a lamb and a bird, but a mother who could not afford a lamb could bring “two turtledoves or two young pigeons” (Leviticus 12:8). Joseph and Mary brought the offering of the poor.

scene.label: “The Consolation of Israel”
scene.text: Simeon was waiting for God to comfort His people, as Isaiah had promised: “Comfort, yes, comfort My people!” (Isaiah 40:1). Devout Jews longed and prayed for that day.

scene.label: A light to the Gentiles
scene.text: Simeon’s words echo Isaiah 49:6, where God’s Servant is given “as a light to the Gentiles.” In the temple courts, at the heart of Israel’s worship, an old Jewish man says that this Child is for the nations too.

scene.label: Anna
scene.text: Anna belonged to Asher, one of the northern tribes scattered by Assyria seven centuries earlier, yet her family still knew its tribe. Luke’s Greek can mean that she was about eighty-four, or that she had been a widow for eighty-four years, which would make her over a hundred.

witnesses.luke: Only Luke tells of Simeon and Anna. He often pairs a man and a woman, as with Zacharias and Mary, and here two aged, faithful witnesses greet Jesus in the temple. Simeon’s word about “a light to bring revelation to the Gentiles” points ahead to Luke’s second book, where the gospel goes out to the nations.

seeing.reveals: Jesus is God’s salvation in person. Simeon held a baby and said, “my eyes have seen Your salvation.” He is light for the nations and glory for Israel, and He will also be a sign spoken against, dividing hearts.
seeing.living: Simeon and Anna had waited for years in prayer and worship, and they recognized God’s salvation in a poor family’s baby. Simeon could face death in peace because he had seen Jesus. That peace is still found in Him, not in having everything else settled.
seeing.ponder: What are you waiting for from God, and is Jesus Himself enough for you to say, “my eyes have seen Your salvation”?

preaching.big_idea: Simeon held God’s salvation in his arms: light for the nations, and a sign spoken against.
outline: A Child who will divide hearts (33–35)
A widow who spoke of Him (36–38)
preaching.watch_for: The law is mentioned four times in verses 22–27, and the Holy Spirit three times in verses 25–27. In this scene the law and the Spirit meet, and both lead to Jesus.
